title: Only part of the branch subnet is reachable
scenario: After a route change, a user can reach branch host 10.20.30.50 but not 10.20.30.200. Both hosts share the intended /24, have verified local connectivity, and previously worked from this source. R1's current output and the change record follow.

exhibits.title: R1 destination lookup
exhibits.text:
Routing entry for 10.20.30.128/25
Known via "static", distance 1, metric 0
Routing Descriptor Blocks:
* directly connected, via Null0

exhibits.title: Change record
exhibits.text:
Added: ip route 10.20.30.128 255.255.255.128 Null0
Intended policy: all of 10.20.30.0/24 remains reachable through the branch router

question: Which change explains the split result?
options: The /24 OSPF metric is compared directly with the static metric.
The new /25 discard overrides the /24 for the .200 destination
The /24 route cannot coexist with a /25 in one routing table
The /25 is less preferred because the /24 was learned first.
explanation: The .200 address lies inside 10.20.30.128/25; .50 does not. The more-specific static sends .200 to Null0 while the /24 continues to serve .50. This is longest prefix match, not a comparison between static and OSPF distances.
fix:
```ios R1
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# no ip route 10.20.30.128 255.255.255.128 Null0
R1(config)# end
R1# show ip route 10.20.30.200
```
Confirm that the /24 is now selected, then test both .50 and .200 from the affected source. Verify replies and save the corrected configuration after the intended policy is restored.

title: The intended backup link is preferred
scenario: Traffic for 10.60.0.0/16 uses the backup path through 10.0.99.2. The intended primary is OSPF. Both next hops are reachable. A protocol inspection confirms a currently eligible OSPF candidate for exactly 10.60.0.0/16 with distance 110 and cost 20; the selected table entry is shown below.

exhibits.title: Verified candidate and next-hop observations
exhibits.text:
OSPF candidate: 10.60.0.0/16, AD 110, cost 20, via 10.0.12.2
10.0.12.2: resolved and reachable
10.0.99.2: resolved and reachable
Required policy: OSPF primary, static backup

question: What makes the backup preferred?
options: Equal-distance paths are load-sharing, and this flow selected the backup.
OSPF must be absent whenever a static line is configured.
The static command uses default AD 1, which beats OSPF 110
The OSPF cost must be lower than the static metric of zero
explanation: The candidates describe the same /16, so source preference applies. The static command omits an AD override and uses 1. Its metric is not compared directly with the OSPF metric. The separate exact-prefix candidate evidence establishes that a usable OSPF alternative exists.
fix:
```ios R1
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# no ip route 10.60.0.0 255.255.0.0 10.0.99.2
R1(config)# ip route 10.60.0.0 255.255.0.0 10.0.99.2 130
R1(config)# end
R1# show ip route 10.60.0.0
R1# show running-config | include ^ip route
```
With the stated OSPF candidate still eligible, its AD 110 is preferred over 130. Verify the selected source and traffic in both directions. A planned failure test must separately establish that the backup remains eligible and actually forwards when the primary is withdrawn.
